'''Marcus Garrett''' (born November 9, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Skyliners Frankfurt]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]].

==Early life==
Garrett began playing [[basketball]] at the age of four.<ref name="wixon" /> He grew up playing basketball, [[association football|soccer]] and [[baseball]] but mainly focused on [[American football|football]]. However, he quit football after breaking his right leg in sixth grade.<ref name="galloway">{{cite web |last1=Galloway |first1=Matt |title='He's a tough hombre, man': How discipline, heartbreak shaped KU basketball's Marcus Garrett |url=https://www.cjonline.com/sports/20180322/hes-tough-hombre-man-how-discipline-heartbreak-shaped-ku-basketballs-marcus-garrett |website=[[The Topeka Capital-Journal]] |accessdate=March 5, 2020 |date=March 22, 2018}}</ref> As a result, Garrett shifted his attention to basketball and began being coached by his uncle and former [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State]] basketball player, Matt Watts. In eighth grade, he joined Watts' [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) team, Swag House, with whom he competed against high school juniors and seniors.<ref name="wixon">{{cite web |last1=Wixon |first1=Matt |title=How Kansas signee Marcus Garrett met his coach's great expectations to lead Skyline to brink of a state title |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/2017/03/09/how-kansas-signee-marcus-garrett-met-his-coach-s-great-expectations-to-lead-skyline-to-brink-of-a-state-title/ |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |accessdate=March 5, 2020 |date=March 8, 2017}}</ref>

Garrett played for [[Skyline High School (Dallas)|Skyline High School]] in [[Dallas|Dallas, Texas]] and grew from 6'2" as a freshman.<ref name="wixon" /> In his senior season, he averaged 17.3 points, 10.4 rebounds, 9.1 assists, 3.1 steals and 2.9 blocks per game, leading his team to the Class 6A state semifinals and earning Texas [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] honors.<ref name="riddle">{{cite web |last1=Riddle |first1=Greg |title=Kansas signee Marcus Garrett of Skyline is named Gatorade Texas Boys Basketball Player of the Year |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/2017/03/20/kansas-signee-marcus-garrett-of-skyline-is-named-gatorade-texas-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year/ |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |accessdate=March 5, 2020 |date=March 20, 2017}}</ref> Garrett was a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top-ranked prospects from Texas in the 2017 class. He committed to playing college basketball for [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] over [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] and [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]], among others.<ref name="signing">{{cite web |title=Kansas basketball lands Marcus Garrett in early signing period |url=https://kuathletics.com/mens-basketball-kansas-basketball-lands-marcus-garrett-in-early-signing-period/ |publisher=Kansas Jayhawks |accessdate=March 5, 2020 |date=November 10, 2016}}</ref>

==College career==
In his freshman season at Kansas, Garrett averaged 4.1 points, 3.4 rebounds and 1.1 assists in 19.2 minutes per game. He emerged as a defensive specialist for the Jayhawks but was deemed their "weak link" on the offensive end as he was not a good three-point shooter.<ref name="goodwin">{{cite web |last1=Goodwin |first1=Shaun |title=Marcus Garrett proving a weak link in Kansas offense |url=http://www.kansan.com/sports/goodwin-marcus-garrett-proving-a-weak-link-in-kansas-offense/article_aa47c002-f5c6-11e7-b17d-0373626616a0.html |website=[[The University Daily Kansan]] |accessdate=March 13, 2020 |date=January 10, 2018}}</ref><ref name="newell">{{cite web |last1=Newell |first1=Jesse |title=KU guard Marcus Garrett is thriving in one stat. Will that lead to more playing time? |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article200405474.html |website=[[The Kansas City Star]] |accessdate=March 13, 2020 |date=February 15, 2018}}</ref> On November 13, 2017, he shared [[Big 12 Conference]] Newcomer of the Week honors with [[Mohamed Bamba]], after posting 10 points and 10 rebounds in a 92–56 win over [[Tennessee State Tigers basketball|Tennessee State]].<ref name="moyle">{{cite web |last1=Moyle |first1=Nick |title=Texas freshman Mo Bamba earns Big 12 newcomer award |url=https://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/college_sports/longhorns/article/Texas-freshman-Mo-Bamba-earns-Big-12-newcomer-12353774.php |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |accessdate=March 13, 2020 |date=November 13, 2017}}</ref> In his sophomore season, Garrett improved as a decision-maker, which helped him earn more playing time.<ref name="cunningham">{{cite web |last1=Cunningham |first1=Dylan |title=The development of Garrett provides another weapon for KU men's basketball |url=http://www.kansan.com/sports/the-development-of-garrett-provides-another-weapon-for-ku-men/article_a5d96d88-1e59-11e9-9fbc-83bc2b1f7385.html |website=[[The University Daily Kansan]] |accessdate=March 13, 2020 |date=January 22, 2019}}</ref> He missed six games in February 2019 with a high ankle sprain.<ref name="bedore">{{cite web |last1=Bedore |first1=Gary |title=Marcus Garrett likely to miss KU-WVU game: 'May be weeks away from being 100 percent' |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article226179210.html |website=[[The Kansas City Star]] |accessdate=March 13, 2020 |date=February 12, 2019}}</ref> At the end of the season, Garrett was named to the [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] All-Defensive Team after averaging 7.3 points, 4.2 rebounds and 1.4 steals per game.<ref name="chasen">{{cite web |last1=Chasen |first1=Scott |title=Marcus Garrett, Devon Dotson receive Big 12 honors |url=https://247sports.com/college/kansas/Article/Marcus-Garrett-Devon-Dotson-of-KU-basketball-receive-Big-12-awards-129924918/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=March 13, 2020 |date=March 10, 2019}}</ref> On February 15, 2020, Garrett scored a career-high 24 points with six three-pointers, five rebounds, seven assists and four steals in an 87–70 win over [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Tait |first1=Matt |title=Marcus Garrett nets 6 triples, No. 3 Kansas overwhelms Oklahoma in 87-70 win |url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2020/feb/15/marcus-garrett-nets-6-triples-no-3-kansas-overwhel/ |publisher=KUSports |accessdate=March 13, 2020 |date=February 15, 2020}}</ref> As a junior, he averaged 9.2 points, 4.6 assists, 4.5 rebounds and 1.8 steals per game and started in all 31 games. He was named Big 12 Defensive Player of the Year while also earning All-Defensive and third-team All-Big 12 accolades.<ref>{{cite web |title=Men's Basketball All-Big 12 Awards Announced |url=https://big12sports.com/news/2020/3/7/mens-basketball-all-big-12-awards-announced.aspx |publisher=[[Big 12 Conference]] |accessdate=March 13, 2020 |date=March 8, 2020}}</ref> On April 1, 2020, Garrett was named the [[Naismith Defensive Player of the Year Award]] winner.<ref>{{Cite web|last =Norlander |first=Matt |title = Kansas' Marcus Garrett, Baylor's DiDi Richards named Naismith Men's and Women's Defensive Player of the Year| work=CBSSports.com| date = April 1, 2020 | url = https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/kansas-marcus-garrett-baylors-didi-richards-named-naismith-mens-and-womens-defensive-player-of-the-year/| accessdate = April 1, 2020}}</ref> As a senior, he averaged 11 points, 4.6 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.6 steals per game.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Bedore |first1=Gary |title=KU's Marcus Garrett isn't taken in NBA Draft but former Jayhawk Quentin Grimes is |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article253135003.html |access-date=December 29, 2021 |work=[[The Kansas City Star]] |date=July 30, 2021}}</ref> Garrett was named to the Second Team All-Big 12 and the Big 12 All-Defensive Team.<ref name=heat/> On April 21, 2021, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his extra year of college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web |last=Campbell | first=Marleah |title=KU's Marcus Garrett declares for NBA Draft |url=https://www.wibw.com/2021/04/22/kus-marcus-garrett-declares-for-nba-draft/ |website=[[WIBW-TV]] |access-date=May 30, 2021 |date=April 21, 2021}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Miami Heat (2021–2022)===
After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Garrett joined the [[Miami Heat]] for the 2021 [[NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2021 Miami HEAT Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-announce-summer-league-roster-2021|website=NBA.com|date=August 1, 2021|access-date=September 11, 2021}}</ref> On September 2, 2021, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Heat. Under the terms of the deal, he split time between the Heat and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].<ref name=heat>{{cite web|title=HEAT Signs Marcus Garrett To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-marcus-garrett-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=September 2, 2021|access-date=September 2, 2021}}</ref> On January 16, 2022, Garrett was waived by the Heat.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Miami HEAT on Twitter: "OFFICIAL. The Miami HEAT have waived Marcus Garrett. He will undergo a season-ending operation to fix the instability in his right wrist."|url=https://twitter.com/MiamiHEAT/status/1482768806930010112|access-date=January 16, 2022|website=Twitter}}</ref>

On July 16, 2022, Garrett re-signed with the Heat on a two-way contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 16, 2022 |title=HEAT SIGN DAYS AND GARRETT TO TWO-WAY CONTRACTS |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-days-and-garrett-to-two-way-contracts-071622 |access-date=July 16, 2022 |website=NBA}}</ref> He was waived on October 13 after he fractured his wrist.

===Sioux Falls Skyforce (2022–2023)===
On October 24, 2022, Garrett rejoined the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] roster for training camp.<ref>{{cite web|title=Charge 2022 Training Camp Roster|url=https://canton.gleague.nba.com/news/charge-2022-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 24, 2022}}</ref>

===Greensboro Swarm (2023–2025)===
On September 26, 2023, Garrett signed with [[Riesen Ludwigsburg|MHP Riesen Ludwigsburg]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]] and the [[Basketball Champions League|Champions League]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Verstärkung vor dem Start: Marcus Garrett|url=https://mhp-riesen-ludwigsburg.de/news/verstaerkung-vor-dem-start-marcus-garrett/|website=MHP-Riesen-Ludwigsburg.de|date=September 26, 2023|access-date=September 28, 2023|language=German}}</ref> but didn't play for them. On December 11, he joined the [[Greensboro Swarm]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Swarm Complete Multiple Transactions|url=https://greensboro.gleague.nba.com/news/swarm-complete-multiple-transactions|website=NBA.com|date=December 11, 2023|access-date=December 11, 2023}}</ref>

On September 11, 2024, Garrett signed with the [[Charlotte Hornets]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Hornets Sign Marcus Garrett, Keyontae Johnson, Caleb McConnell And Joel Soriano|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-sign-marcus-garrett-keyontae-johnson-caleb-mcconnell-and-joel-soriano|website=NBA.com|date=September 11, 2024|access-date=September 11, 2024}}</ref> but was waived on October 2.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hornets Acquire Three Picks, Three Players In Three-Team Trade|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-acquire-three-picks-three-players-in-three-team-trade|website=NBA.com|date=October 2, 2024|access-date=October 3, 2024}}</ref> On October 27, he re-joined Greensboro.<ref>{{cite web|title=Greensboro Swarm Announce Training Camp Roster for 2024-25 Season|url=https://greensboro.gleague.nba.com/news/greensboro-swarm-announce-training-camp-roster-for-2024-25-season|website=NBA.com|date=October 27, 2024|access-date=October 27, 2024}}</ref>

===Charlotte Hornets (2025)===
On March 12, 2025, Garrett signed a 10-day contract with the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-sign-marcus-garrett-to-10-day-contract |title=Hornets Sign Marcus Garrett to 10-Day Contract |website=NBA.com |publisher=Charlotte Hornets |date=March 12, 2025 |access-date=March 19, 2025}}</ref> However, when his contract expired on March 22, he was not re-signed by the team.
